about.title: Greenfield Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey County residents rely on a limited set of local clinics and hospitals, which means many Greenfield families already know their providers personally — making a suspected medical error feel even more disorienting. Whether the issue involved a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error, California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim. Under MICRA, strict notice periods and expert-review requirements apply, and a poor medical result by itself doesn't automatically mean negligence occurred. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your case ourselves — we simply connect Greenfield residents with an independent attorney in our network who can review the details, explain your options, and help you understand whether the timeline and evidence support moving forward. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to proceed afterward. If you're unsure whether what happened to you crosses the line into malpractice, talking with someone who handles these claims regularly is often the clearest way to find out.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Documentation Matter in Greenfield

items.title: Strict Filing Windows Apply
items.desc: California generally requires a malpractice claim to be filed within one year of discovering the injury, and no later than three years from when it occurred. Waiting to sort things out can quietly close the door on a valid claim.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can even be filed, California law typically requires sending the healthcare provider a 90-day advance notice. An attorney familiar with this step can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad medical outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, a qualified medical expert generally has to weigh in on whether the standard of care was violated. Connecting with an attorney who works with the right specialists can be the difference in how a case moves forward.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment at a Greenfield clinic — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result on its own doesn't establish negligence. What matters is whether the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, which is typically determined through medical expert review.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after a medical error?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the general rule is one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it happened. Because Greenfield residents sometimes continue treatment with the same limited pool of local providers, discovery of an error can be delayed — so it's worth having a timeline reviewed early.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap adjusts upward each year under current law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to this same cap.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We are not a law firm and don't handle or evaluate your claim ourselves.
